blocks.en: We now state a theorem on the relationship between the adjoint of an operator and its closure.
blocks.zh: 现在陈述一个关于算子的伴随与其闭包之间关系的定理.

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.en: Let $(\mathcal{D}(A),A)$ be an operator from $X$ to $Y$ with dense domain. Then the adjoint operator $A^\times$ is closed. Furthermore, if $X$ and $Y$ are reflexive Banach spaces, then $(\mathcal{D}(A),A)$ is closable if and only if $\mathcal{D}(A^\times)$ is dense, in which case $\overline A=A^{\times\times}$.
blocks.zh: 设 $(\mathcal{D}(A),A)$ 为从 $X$ 到 $Y$ 的稠密定义域算子. 那么伴随算子 $A^\times$ 是闭的. 此外, 若 $X$ 和 $Y$ 是自反 Banach 空间, 则 $(\mathcal{D}(A),A)$ 可闭, 当且仅当 $\mathcal{D}(A^\times)$ 稠密, 此时 $\overline A=A^{\times\times}$.
blocks.label: thm:adjoint-closedness-and-double-adjoint-closure

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.en:
To show that $A^\times$ is closed we use Lemma~\ref{lem:closed-operator-sequential-criterion}. That is, suppose there is a sequence $v_n$ in $\mathcal{D}(A^\times)\subset Y^*$ such that $v_n\to v$ for some $v\in Y^*$ and $A^\times v_n\to f$ for some $f\in X^*$. We need to show that $v(Au)=f(u)$ for every $u\in\mathcal{D}(A)$. But since convergence in $Y^*$ $(X^*)$ implies weak-* convergence in $Y^*$ $(X^*)$, we have\[v(Au)=\lim_{n\to\infty}v_n(Au)=\lim_{n\to\infty}A^\times v_n(u)=f(u)\]for any $u\in\mathcal{D}(A)$. Thus, $A^\times$ is closed.

The rest of the proof is left to the reader (Problem~\ref{ex:adjoint-closure-theorem-proof-completion}).
blocks.zh:
为证明 $A^\times$ 是闭的, 使用 Lemma~\ref{lem:closed-operator-sequential-criterion}. 即假设 $\mathcal{D}(A^\times)\subset Y^*$ 中存在序列 $v_n$, 使得对某个 $v\in Y^*$ 有 $v_n\to v$, 且对某个 $f\in X^*$ 有 $A^\times v_n\to f$. 需要证明, 对每个 $u\in\mathcal{D}(A)$ 均有 $v(Au)=f(u)$. 但由于 $Y^*$ $(X^*)$ 中的收敛蕴含 $Y^*$ $(X^*)$ 中的弱-* 收敛, 对任意 $u\in\mathcal{D}(A)$ 均有\[v(Au)=\lim_{n\to\infty}v_n(Au)=\lim_{n\to\infty}A^\times v_n(u)=f(u)\]因而 $A^\times$ 是闭的.

证明的其余部分留给读者 (Problem~\ref{ex:adjoint-closure-theorem-proof-completion}).
